content: 1. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of amitriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of amoxapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Chloroquine decreases the levels of ampicillin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 4. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of apomorphine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of arformoterol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Both asenapine (transdermal) and chloroquine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 9. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval, and chloroquine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates as per prescribing information. 12. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to the total analgesic effect. 13. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 14. Chloroquine and bupivacaine implant may increase each other's effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Local anesthetics may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when combined with drugs that also cause this condition. 15. Bupropion increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 17. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Chloroquine decreases the effects of cholera vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer the cholera vaccine at least 10 days before starting antimalarial prophylaxis with chloroquine. 20. Both chloroquine and ciprofloxacin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but caution is advised when used with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 21. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of citalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Clobazam increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lower doses of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6 may be required when used concomitantly. 23. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and increases its toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clozapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of codeine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to the active metabolite morphine. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Crizotinib increases the levels of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine also increases the toxicity of crizotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. 28. Crofelemer increases the levels of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer minimally inhibits CYP3A4 systemically but may inhibit it in the gut. 29. Chloroquine increases the levels of cyclosporine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of dasatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of desipramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and increases its toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of deutetrabenazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death with QTc-prolonging drugs. 34. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of dolasetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of doxepin by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of droperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 40. Eliglustat increases the levels of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the concomitant drug. 41. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of encorafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of escitalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP2D6 substrates as necessary. 47. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of flecainide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and increases its toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of fluconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Both chloroquine and fostemsavir increase the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Both chloroquine and gadobenate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Both chloroquine and gemtuzumab increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Goserelin increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval and increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Chloroquine decreases the effects of Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible. Revaccinate patients 3 months after therapy if immune competence is restored. 55. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and increases its toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Histrelin increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval and increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to the total analgesic effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of hydromorphone by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Iloperidone increases the levels of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Chloroquine decreases the effects of influenza virus vaccine (trivalent, recombinant) by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of inotuzumab by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Lanthanum carbonate decreases the levels of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer chloroquine at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Both chloroquine and lenvatinib increase the QTc interval. Monitor ECG closely when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval and increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lofexidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Lorcaserin increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 75. Magaldrate decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 76. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 77. Magnesium oxide decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 78. Both chloroquine and mavorixafor increase the QTc interval. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 79. Chloroquine decreases the effects of meningococcal group B vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Individuals with altered immunocompetence may have reduced immune responses to the vaccine.
